dominos.why: Item 19 prints average weekly unit sales (AWUS); the calculator works on a year, so the weekly average and median are multiplied by 52 and the label says so.

headline.label: Average weekly unit sales of franchised traditional stores open all of 2025 ($27,267), times 52 weeks

chick-fil-a.why: Item 6: the Operator pays 15 % of gross receipts (equipment rental and the business services fee are taken out of it, so they are not counted again) plus 50 % of the restaurant's net profit.

kfc.why: Item 6, note 2: a new outlet of a franchisee who is not a Legacy Franchisee pays 5 % (4 % for Legacy Franchisees, 5.25 % under a Brand Contribution Option); the calculator uses the rate of a new franchisee.

little-caesars.why: Item 6 prints the advertising fee only as 'up to 7 %' of gross sales, as decided by the franchisor; the calculator uses that maximum and the page says it is a ceiling.

f45.why: Item 6: the $2,500 monthly minimum royalty is already covered by the 7 % rate in the calculator, and merchandise and heart-rate bands are purchases, not fees; the fixed fees counted are the $2,500 monthly marketing fee and the $500 monthly technology fee.

fixedYear.note: Marketing Fee $2,500 a month, Technology Service Fee $500 a month

mathnasium.why: Item 6: besides 10 % of gross receipts, a $650 monthly base royalty, a $250 monthly fixed marketing fee, a digital and local marketing fee of at least $1,000 a month and a $266 monthly technology fee; the convention ticket is left out.

fixedYear.note: Base Royalty $650 a month, Marketing Fee fixed part $250 a month, Digital and Local Marketing Fee $1,000 a month minimum, Technology License Fee $266 a month

anytime-fitness.why: Item 6: the royalty is a flat monthly fee; the calculator counts the $842 monthly fee, the $900 advertising fee and the $799 technology fee, not the $1,000 monthly Club Enhancement reserve, which is a recommended set-aside.

fixedYear.note: Monthly Fee (royalty) $842, General Advertising and Marketing Fee $900, Base Technology Fee $799, each a month

snap-fitness.why: Item 6: the royalty is a flat monthly fee; the calculator counts the fees paid to the franchisor or its funds ($725 royalty, $518 national marketing, $450 technology, $200 local fund, each a month), not insurance premiums or recommended local spending.

fixedYear.note: Royalty Fee $725, National Marketing $518, Technology Fee $450, Local Marketing Fund $200, each a month

jets-pizza.why: Item 6: the royalty is 12 % of what the franchisee spends on inventory and supplies, not a share of sales, and the current ad fund rate is not printed; the model cannot represent it without guessing, so the brand is left out.

kumon.why: Item 6: the royalty is a flat amount per enrolled student and subject, which depends on enrollment the document does not give as an average; left out rather than guessed.

servpro.why: Item 6: the royalty slides from 10 % to 3 % with monthly volume, plus a fixed fee and a minimum, and no Item 19 is published; left out rather than guessed.

chem-dry.why: Item 19 is a projection for one van, not actual sales, the royalty is tiered with minimums and the ad fund is printed only as 'up to 3 %'; left out rather than guessed.

freddys.why: Item 6: the advertising fund contribution rises from 2.5 % to 3 % of gross sales as of October 8, 2026, a date already passed; the calculator uses 3 %.

popeyes.why: Item 6, note 4: restaurants in the Ad Fund Test Program, including all new franchisees, pay an advertising contribution of 5 % starting April 1, 2025 (4.6 % if the test fails); the calculator uses 5 %.

valvoline.why: Item 6: the General System Fund takes up to 2 % of adjusted gross revenue only until a yearly cap of $7,344 per center is reached; at the sales Item 19 reports the cap binds, so the calculator counts the fund as the $7,344 fixed amount and not as a percentage.

fixedYear.note: General System Fund, capped at $7,344 a year
